adrs: Microsoft Entra External ID browser-redirect OIDC is the target identity profile, but APBRA-162 uses only an Entra-compatible provider adapter and deterministic local/CI test issuer; no live tenant or credentials are required

External authentication establishes identity only; APBRA-owned invitations, company memberships, capabilities and private-resource grants remain authoritative and are re-evaluated on every protected operation

Initial application roles are COMPANY_OWNER, COMPANY_ADMIN, MEMBER and EXPERT unless implementation inspection proves an equivalent existing canonical role; only owner or admin capability may issue invitations, and role labels never replace resource authorization

Company creation and the first owner use an explicit server-side development and test bootstrap; no public registration, email-domain ownership inference, client-selected company identifier or client-selected owner role is accepted
One FastAPI and Pydantic modular-monolith API sits behind the existing React and Vite frontend; domain and application responsibilities remain independent of HTTP, OIDC and SQLAlchemy provider types
PostgreSQL 17, SQLAlchemy 2.x, explicit Alembic migrations and psycopg 3 provide durable state; SQLite and in-memory substitutes cannot prove PostgreSQL behavior

Authlib with its cryptography dependency provides the standards-based OIDC and signed JWT adapter boundary; implementation versions are exact-locked and provider-specific claims stay behind that adapter

Browser authentication uses the OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE S256, exact allowlisted redirects, transaction-bound state and nonce, issuer mix-up protection and one-time callback consumption; provider tokens remain server-side and the browser receives only a protected APBRA session credential

Invitations use cryptographically strong non-enumerable bearer secrets, persist only a one-way cryptographic digest, are single-use, expire after a configurable server-side default of seven days, bind one validated issuer and subject to the exact invited company membership, and never expose raw secrets in database rows, logs, audit events, UI history, fixtures or repository content

Cases have stable identity, immutable original request versions, a mutable current-version pointer, optimistic concurrency, payload-bound idempotency and transaction-consistent state and audit evidence

APBRA-162 is local and CI only with AUD 0 cloud spend, synthetic data and offline provider substitutes; no Azure resource, live Entra integration, paid model call, customer data or hosted endpoint is authorized
Azure Blob Storage and Australia East are future hosted directions only; APBRA-162 implements no object storage, upload, candidate download or cloud provisioning

acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test issuer proves the same signature, exact issuer, audience, expiry and subject validation boundary intended for Entra External ID; tests do not inject a pre-authorized actor or treat client company, role or capability claims as authority.

The browser redirect boundary uses authorization code plus PKCE S256, transaction-bound unpredictable state and nonce, exact allowlisted redirect targets, issuer mix-up protection and one-time callback handling; wrong or reused state, nonce, issuer, code, redirect or verifier and PKCE downgrade all fail closed.

OIDC provider tokens and refresh credentials remain server-side and never enter browser storage, frontend bundles, URLs, logs or API responses; the APBRA browser session is protected against script access and cross-site request abuse, and local/CI cookie exceptions cannot weaken a later hosted profile.

An explicitly server-bootstrapped COMPANY_OWNER or COMPANY_ADMIN can issue a single-use invitation with a configurable server-side seven-day default expiry; MEMBER and EXPERT cannot issue invitations merely from their role, and no client-selected company identifier or owner role is authoritative.

Valid invitation acceptance binds the validated issuer and subject to the exact invited company membership; expired, revoked, replayed and cross-company use fails, concurrent or repeated acceptance is idempotent for the same binding or returns an explicit conflict, and consumption plus membership creation is one transaction.

Invitation tokens have sufficient cryptographic entropy, persist only as a one-way digest, use timing-safe secret verification where application comparison occurs, and never appear raw in database rows, audit evidence, logs, errors, fixtures, UI history or API responses after initial issuance.

Every protected operation resolves the validated external identity binding and re-evaluates active membership, capabilities and private-resource access; unknown identities, deactivated memberships, removed company members and revoked case access fail immediately even if the external token remains valid.

An invited active member can use the actual UI to create a private reporting case with a natural-language original request and without a project or file, through the real API and migrated PostgreSQL database.

A case has a stable server-generated ID, server-derived company and creator, immutable initial request version, current-version pointer, audit evidence and optimistic concurrency version, with state and audit committed transactionally.

Database constraints and transaction checks preserve company consistency across identities, memberships, invitations, cases, access grants, request versions, idempotency and audit rows; a foreign-company identifier cannot create a cross-tenant relation even if application input is forged.

The user can list only cases currently authorized to them and resume an authorized case after browser refresh, frontend restart, API restart and PostgreSQL-backed restart without losing original request or version history.

Equivalent repeated create commands under the same payload-bound idempotency key return the same logical case, while a different payload under the same key conflicts and does not create or mutate a second case.
Stale updates fail with a recoverable conflict and cannot overwrite the current version; earlier business submissions remain immutable when the current case changes.
Foreign-company and ungranted same-company private-case reads and writes use consistent non-enumerating protected-resource errors that do not reveal or disclose case existence or protected details.

PostgreSQL 17 integration tests run migrations from an empty database and exercise database constraints, foreign keys, uniqueness, transactions, idempotency, concurrency and restart persistence without substituting SQLite or in-memory persistence.

The existing conversational shell operates against the persisted case without rewriting clarification, ConfirmedRequirementContract, ReportDesign, compiler or deterministic candidate-validation behavior, and a description-only case does not imply factual generation readiness.

Four unrelated synthetic business-domain descriptions and renamed fields exercise the same case and authorization path with no production branch on scenario, fixture, prompt, filename, KPI, table, column or visual arrangement.

The signed-in shell, invite acceptance, case list, create and resume flows plus forbidden, expired-session and recoverable-conflict states are tested through component paths, and one browser test exercises the real UI to API to PostgreSQL journey rather than a mocked service.

No object storage, upload, PBIP persistence or download, report-generation API, expert assignment, project sharing, public registration, billing, cloud provisioning, hosted exposure, social login, compiler change or production RAG capability is implemented or presented as complete.

All dependencies are exact-locked and reviewed; runtime families are FastAPI, Pydantic and pydantic-settings, SQLAlchemy 2.x, Alembic, psycopg 3, Authlib with cryptography and Uvicorn, with pytest, HTTPX, Ruff, mypy and Playwright used only where justified; changing the driver or OIDC/JWT family requires renewed authority and review.

The sole bootstrap-test implementation permission is tests/bootstrap/test_bootstrap.py and is limited to changing p.parent.mkdir(parents=True) to p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) inside test_product_file_is_not_bootstrap; its rejection assertion and every other test behavior remain unchanged, and every other tests/bootstrap file remains outside implementation authority.

Haseeb remains manual merge authority; registration and implementation are separate, and no application implementation begins until the registration PR is manually merged and current main is refreshed.
